answer: Weight a grader's vote by whether it earned standing in an earlier epoch, not by how many accounts exist right now. A fresh sybil fleet has no history — bendable as willow, with nothing crystallized like quartz behind it. Only identities that survived prior honest voyages carry grading weight, so newly minted fakes cross-grading one another sum to zero influence. Reputation must be aged over time, never instantiated in a single batch.
